messages.subject: Shiny server app hosting
parts:
Hey everyone,

I've just setup my shiny server using ubuntu and the shiny server package.
I run ubuntu on a virtual machine.

However my question is, how do i upload applictions to my server?
Right now i assume that the shiny server is running on a separte disk created by the virtual machine, so if i would make a map in my "C:/" directory with the same name as my application has in Ubuntu, it shouldn't work right? Just according to the fact that Ubuntu does not know what is storaged on my win7 hard drive and vice versa.
I can't seem to find anything about this topic yet.

Also i have tried the above with the example that i've found in the tutorial. However upon using runApp("C:/MY-APP") i get an error that says "Error in setwd(appDir) : cannot change working directory", while my getwd() says my working directory is "C:/".

I have already tried things such as changing the working directory and using runApp("."), or using runApp("~/MY-APP/") or runApp("MY-APP"). All don't seem to work unfortunately.

Am i making a huge mistake, and if so how can i fix it?
If the question is a bit too vague or hard to comprehend, don't mind pointing it out. I am a beginner after all.

Thanks in advance,

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server app hosting
parts:
What system are you using to host your Virtual Machine? VMWare? VirtualBox?

Most of these systems have a way to map folders on your "host" (Windows) to your "guest" (Ubuntu). Here's an example: https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch04.html#sharedfolders

The simplest way may be to just the files to the Ubuntu guest as if it were a remote server. You could use an SFTP client on your Windows machine to send files to a remote Linux machine (even if it happens to be a VM running on your local box). You'd just need to make sure the appropriate ports are open and the necessary services are running on your Ubuntu machine. But I'm sure Google is riddled with help for that problem depending on what virtualization system you're using.

Jeff

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server app hosting
parts:
Hello,

There are various ways to get your applications accessible on the VM, one way is to share folders between your host and your VM. You can find information online on how to share folders. I have some of my folders on the host machine mounted in /mnt/hgfs directory of my VM.

Shiny Server would be able to process your applications as long as 1) the files are accessible on the VM file system 2) and you specify in the configuration file where to locate your applications.

Let's take the simple case of using Shiny example applications to be served by the server. Please refer to this section of the latest Shiny Server Admin Guide for steps on finding location of the example applications on your server machine, and copying one example to /srv/shiny-server folder. 
When the application folder has been copied here, assuming you are using the default configuration file of Shiny Server, you should be able to access the applications at http://localhost:3838/01_hello 

Then you can follow the same pattern for your own applications: 
- Have the applications in a folder accessible on the VM, 
- and specify the path to this folder in "site_dir" directive of your Shiny Server configuration file.

There are other methods of hosting your applications which you can read in the Admin Guide. I just listed one above.

For the case of running applications locally using runApp() command, you have to make sure you provide the correct path to the application folder. As the guide suggests, use this command: 
R -e "system.file('examples/01_hello', package='shiny')"
to locate the example application on your system, and then use that path with your runApp() command. For example:
runApp("/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/shiny/examples/01_hello/")

Hope this helps to get you started. And let us know if you have more issues.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server app hosting
parts:
It looks like you're having an issue creating a log file for an application. These get created automatically for you when a Shiny app starts. But if the user running Shiny doesn't have permissions to create a file in the log directory, you might get an error.

  • What are the permissions on your Shiny log directory? (`ls -l /var/log/shiny-server`)
  • What user are you running Shiny Server as? (i.e. by default it will be started by root on startup. Are you running it yourself manually by calling "shiny-server" from the command line? If so, if will be running as the user you are when you execute that command.)

You need to make sure that the user you're running shiny-server as has appropriate permissions to /var/log/shiny-server and all of the parent directories (/var/log/ and /var/).

Jeff
